steps.u: The nightly sensor CSV ingest sometimes loads rows with humidity > 100 or missing station ids. Add validation to the pipeline and write bad rows to a reject file instead of loading them.

steps.a: I'll define a pandera `DataFrameSchema` and validate lazily so every failing row is collected in one pass, then split valid rows from rejects using `failure_cases.index`.

i.new_string:
df = df.rename(columns=str.lower)
    try:
        SCHEMA.validate(df, lazy=True)
        bad = pd.Index([])
    except pa.errors.SchemaErrors as e:
        bad = pd.Index(e.failure_cases['index'].dropna().unique())
    df.loc[bad].to_csv(out / f"{path.stem}.rejects.csv", index=False)
    good = df.drop(index=bad)
    good.to_parquet(out / f"{path.stem}.parquet", index=False)
    log.info('ingested %d rows, rejected %d', len(good), len(bad))
    return len(good)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SCHEMA = pa.DataFrameSchema({
    'station_id': pa.Column(str, nullable=False),
    'observed_at': pa.Column('datetime64[ns]'),
    'temp_c': pa.Column(float, pa.Check.in_range(-60, 60)),
    'humidity_pct': pa.Column(float, pa.Check.in_range(0, 100)),
})

steps.a: Validation is in: a pandera schema checks station_id non-null, temperature and humidity ranges; failing rows go to `<stem>.rejects.csv`. On the 11-20 sample, 14,397 rows loaded and 3 were rejected; existing ingest tests pass.

reference.summary: Added row-level validation to a pandas CSV ingest pipeline with a pandera schema validated lazily. Rows with a missing station id or out-of-range humidity or temperature go to a rejects CSV, and only valid rows are written to Parquet. On a sample file 14,397 rows loaded and 3 were rejected; existing tests pass.
facts: Pipeline reads sensor CSVs and writes Parquet
Added pandera schema: station_id non-null, humidity 0-100, temp -60..60
Lazy validation collects all failure cases; bad rows go to a rejects CSV

decisions.reason: it collects every failing row in one pass so all rejects can be split out
